extracted.intended_audience: regulated establishments and employers, industry stakeholders and trade groups, labor representatives, economists and policy analysts, and public commenters on the OSHA heat NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Economic analysis and reporting requirements for estimating and tabulating employer compliance costs associated with OSHA's high-heat-trigger protections (tables and methodology for costs by industry and region).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning signs applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA assumed that the cost of placing warning signs for excessively high heat areas is only applicable to industries assumed to have radiant heat sources (as outlined in OSHA, 2024c and discussed in section VIII.C.IV.E.IV.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit warning-sign cost calculations to establishments in industries with radiant heat sources per OSHA's industry assumptions. See discussion referenced (OSHA, 2024c; section VIII.C.IV.E.IV.). OSHA requests comment where evidence suggests other applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign unit-cost calculation (signs)
rubrics_metrics.description: To calculate total costs of this provision, OSHA multiplies the number of affected establishments with radiant heat sources by the unit cost for a warning sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each industry/region, compute sign costs as: number_of_affected_establishments_with_radiant_heat_sources * unit_cost_per_warning_sign. Populate table rows with resulting dollar values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning sign placement unit-cost calculation (designated person)
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA multiplies the number of affected establishments by the unit cost for a designated person to place that warning sign in an excessively high heat area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For personnel/placement costs, compute as: number_of_affected_establishments * unit_cost_for_designated_person. Include these labor-placement costs separately from sign purchase costs in the tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present cost formats: one-time annualized, annual, and total annualized (discounted and undiscounted)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table VIII.C.25. shows the annualized one-time, annual, and total annualized costs for each of these requirements by industry category and region, discounted (2 percent over a 10-year period) and undiscounted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report costs in multiple formats: one-time annualized amounts, recurring annual costs, and total annualized costs. Provide both undiscounted numbers and discounted values using a 2% discount rate over a 10-year horizon (or state the discounting convention used). Clearly label discounted vs undiscounted columns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use best available evidence and state limitations (example: Alaska)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that the best available evidence OSHA employed in this analysis showed no days exceeding the high heat trigger in Alaska and therefore, the agency estimated that most industries in Alaska will not have costs of compliance for requirements at or above the high heat trigger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state data limitations and how they affect estimates (e.g., zero-cost estimates where no days exceeded triggers). Call out potential understating of effects (e.g., in establishments exposed to process heat) and invite commenter-supplied data to adjust estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include rest-breaks cost categories (indoor and outdoor) by industry and region
rubrics_metrics.description: Rest Breaks at High Heat Trigger—Indoor and Rest Breaks at High Heat Trigger—Outdoor are reported with costs by industry category and region (subtotals and totals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate rest-break cost estimates by setting (indoor vs outdoor) and provide detailed industry-by-region breakdowns with subtotals and grand totals. Include one-time vs annualized distinctions per the reporting format above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include observation-for-signs-and-symptoms costs by role
rubrics_metrics.description: Observation for Signs and Symptoms—Designated Person and Observation for Signs and Symptoms—At-Risk Worker are included as distinct cost items with industry/region breakdowns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate and report observation costs separately for designated observers (e.g., assigned employee) and for at-risk workers (e.g., time spent observing peers/self). Provide subtotals by industry and region and clarify whether costs are hourly, per-event, or annualized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include hazard-alert costs separated by timing (initial vs subsequent) and role (supervisor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Hazard Alert—Supervisor and Subsequent Hazard Alert—Supervisor are reported as separate line items with associated costs by industry and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish initial alert actions/costs from subsequent alerts; estimate supervisor time and associated unit costs for each and report industry/region subtotals and totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report warning-sign counts and placement counts by region/industry
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables report counts (and derived costs) for Warning Signs and Signage Placement broken down by region (Alaskan, Central, Eastern, Pacific, Southern, Western) and by industry category with subtotals and totals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When presenting signage-related costs, include both the number of signs (or affected establishments) and the computed dollar costs, broken out by region and industry. Provide subtotals for each industry and regional totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate totals for requirements at or above the high heat trigger
rubrics_metrics.description: Total Costs for Requirements at or above the High Heat Trigger are presented by industry and region (showing one-time annualized, annual, total annualized, discounted and undiscounted values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide final aggregated cost summaries across all included requirements (rest breaks, observation, alerts, signage, placement, etc.), with clear presentation of how line items sum to subtotals and totals. Include both discounted and undiscounted aggregate figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological principle: unit-cost multiplication for requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA's cost calculations rely on multiplying counts (e.g., number of affected establishments) by appropriate unit costs (for signs, designated persons, supervisor time, etc.) to derive total costs for each requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each requirement type, document the count source (how many establishments/workers are affected), the unit cost used, and the multiplication used to derive totals. Make unit-cost assumptions transparent so commenters can supply alternate unit costs or counts.
